definition.name: Tn5-mediated DNA fragmentation and adapter tagging
definition.substrate: DNA-containing material accessible to adapter-loaded Tn5, including DNA in chromatin; material state and prior enrichment are retained on each use.
definition.operation: Couple DNA fragmentation with introduction of sequencing-adapter tags in a Tn5 transposition reaction.
definition.physical_mechanism: Adapter-loaded hyperactive Tn5 transposase fragments substrate DNA and integrates its adapter payload at insertion sites.
definition.output: Tagmented DNA-containing material carrying sequencing-adapter tags, at the reaction-product stage before separately required purification, end completion or PCR; support and protein association are retained as per-use properties.
definition.information_effect: Adds sequencing-adapter sequence at fragmentation/insertion sites while retaining substrate-derived DNA sequence and fragment information for downstream readout. Which genomic regions are represented and what their representation means depend on upstream selection and substrate accessibility, recorded on each use.
definition.purpose: Generate adapter-tagged DNA fragments for subsequent sequencing-library preparation.
definition.context_requirements: Requires DNA, an adapter-loaded Tn5 preparation and conditions permitting the coupled transposition/tagging reaction. Native versus fixed chromatin, prior antibody enrichment, bead attachment, enzyme product, buffer, dose, duration and downstream readout are contextual properties rather than universal membership conditions.

tn5_dna_fragmentation_adapter_tagging.scope_note: A shared-mechanism concept requiring both DNA fragmentation and sequencing-adapter introduction by Tn5. It spans the supplied native-nuclear and immunoprecipitated bead-chromatin implementations without making either the defining substrate. The assigned transformation ends at tagmented material; later washes, crosslink reversal, DNA purification, end completion and amplification remain separate interfaces. RNA reverse transcription with template-switch handle introduction does not meet this mechanism. Membership establishes neither experimental substitution, shared ancestry, literature novelty nor a complete reaction recipe.

definition.name: Reverse transcription with template-switch addition of a PCR handle
definition.substrate: RNA annealed to an extendable DNA primer, with a compatible template-switch oligonucleotide supplied.
definition.operation: Extend the primer to synthesize cDNA from RNA and use template switching to introduce a distal PCR handle in the connected reverse-transcription transformation.
definition.physical_mechanism: Reverse-transcriptase-mediated RNA-templated DNA synthesis coupled to switching to the supplied oligonucleotide template to introduce the distal amplification handle. This is a qualitative mechanism; exact terminal nucleotide and strand intermediates are not specified by the definition.
definition.output: Primer-derived cDNA-bearing material with the initiating primer sequence retained and a template-switch-derived distal PCR handle, before separate primer cleanup or PCR; any primer attachment to a support is retained.
definition.information_effect: Copies RNA sequence into DNA and adds the opposite amplification handle. Pre-existing primer tags remain associated through primer extension; their identity and biological provenance are per-use properties.
definition.purpose: Convert captured RNA into cDNA with handles for subsequent amplification and sequencing-library preparation.
definition.context_requirements: Requires an RNA-primed reverse-transcription system and compatible template-switch oligonucleotide that together yield the distal PCR-handle output. Bead attachment, oligo-dT priming, cellular barcodes, UMIs, bulk execution, enzyme brand, reaction composition and incubation program are contextual implementation properties, not universal membership conditions.

reverse_transcription_template_switch_pc.scope_note: A shared-mechanism concept for the connected RNA-to-cDNA synthesis and template-switch PCR-handle installation, with both actions and their output required for membership. Generic RNA capture, reverse transcription lacking established template switching, Tn5 DNA fragmentation/tagging, and downstream PCR are outside this definition. It is not specific to a bead brand, barcode design or bulk/droplet location. The supplied singleton supports this coherent comparison category; further memberships require their own evidence. Shared mechanism establishes neither experimental substitution, ancestry, novelty nor a complete reaction recipe.
